facts.text: I have a rash.
It's spread widely over my body.
It's made of flat spots and small raised bumps.
I've had a fever.
My muscles ache.
My joints ache.
My urine has been dark.
My skin itches.
I have pain in my belly.
It's in the upper right part of my belly.

facts.item: how long the rash and the other symptoms have lasted
facts.text: The rash, fever, muscle and joint aches, dark urine, itching and belly pain have been going on for 10 days.
My skin and the whites of my eyes have turned yellow.

facts.item: when the rash and yellowing started
facts.text: The rash and the yellowing began about 20 days after I started nevirapine.
I've been feeling nauseated.
I've been vomiting.
I've been eating and drinking less.

facts.item: when the nausea, vomiting and eating less started
facts.text: The nausea, vomiting and eating less started 3 days ago.
I have HIV.
My HIV has been well controlled for the past three years; my CD4 counts have always been above 500.
I take zidovudine for my HIV; I've been on it for the past three years.
I take lamivudine for my HIV; I've been on it for the past three years.
I took lopinavir–ritonavir for my HIV for about three years, until it was replaced 45 days ago.
Forty-five days ago my HIV medicines were changed and I started nevirapine, together with zidovudine and lamivudine.

facts.item: reason the HIV medicines were changed
aliases: side effects of the HIV medicines
facts.text: My HIV medicines were changed because the old combination upset my stomach and bowels.

findings.name: skin examination
findings.result: Marked skin icterus; diffuse maculopapular rash covering >50% of the body surface.

findings.name: abdominal examination
findings.result: Abdomen soft, with tenderness in the right hypochondrium; no hepatosplenomegaly.

findings.name: complete blood count
findings.result: Normal complete blood count and differential.

findings.name: metabolic panel
findings.result: Glucose normal; electrolytes normal; serum creatinine increased threefold; estimated glomerular filtration rate decreased by 75%.

findings.name: liver function tests
findings.result: Elevated aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase and γ-glutamyl transpeptidase.

findings.name: viral hepatitis serology
findings.result: Hepatitis A IgM negative; hepatitis B antibodies negative; hepatitis C antibodies negative.

findings.name: abdominal ultrasound
findings.result: Liver of normal size and shape with homogeneously increased echogenicity of the parenchyma.

aliases: drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
gold.reasoning: 1. Acute viral hepatitis was considered but excluded — “Testing was negative for cytomegalovirus (CMV) antigenemia, antibodies to HBV and HCV, and IgM antibodies to hepatitis A virus.” 2. Primary CMV infection was ruled out — “Testing was negative for cytomegalovirus (CMV) antigenemia…” 3. Drug hypersensitivity was suspected given timing with nevirapine initiation — “she was admitted to our hospital twenty days after initiating the new regimen because of a diffuse maculopapular rash accompanied by discrete yellow discoloration of the whites of the eyes…”

quotes.f011: a 10-day history of diffuse maculopapular rash, fever, myalgias, arthralgias, choluria, pruritus, and right upper-quadrant abdominal pain
quotes.f013: Twenty days after starting nevirapine the rash and jaundice began
quotes.f017: Three days before admission she developed nausea, vomiting, and decreased oral intake
quotes.f019: Her HIV had been well controlled on zidovudine, lamivudine, and lopinavir–ritonavir for the past three years, with CD4 counts consistently >500 cells/mm3
quotes.f022: lopinavir–ritonavir for the past three years
quotes.f023: Forty-five days before presentation her regimen was changed to zidovudine, lamivudine, and nevirapine

f011: The 10-day history (s001) conflicts with the timeline of s004-s005 (nevirapine started 45 days before presentation, rash and jaundice 20 days later, i.e. about 25 days before presentation). Both statements are kept as the source gives them; see source_issues.
f013: Conflicts with the 10-day history in s001 (see f011 and source_issues).
f012: Jaundice is not in the s001 symptom list; it comes from s005 (rash and jaundice began) and the examination (marked conjunctival and skin icterus). The patient can see it.
f024: The source says the regimen was changed because of gastrointestinal intolerance without naming the drug responsible; the fact keeps it at the level of the old combination.

source_issues: Timeline conflict: s001 gives a 10-day history, but s004-s005 place the start of the rash and jaundice 20 days after a nevirapine start 45 days before presentation (about 25 days before presentation). The reasoning quote says she was admitted twenty days after starting the new regimen, which conflicts with s004's 45 days.
The complete blood count and differential are reported normal (no eosinophilia), although the gold diagnosis is DRESS.
Jaundice is reported in s005 and on examination but is not in the presenting symptom list of s001.
notes: Index visit: the admission after 10 days of rash, fever, aches, dark urine, itching and right upper-quadrant pain, with 3 days of nausea and vomiting (s001-s009 all describe this presentation).

The CD4 counts of the past three years are kept both as a test finding (with time) and in the patient's account of how well controlled the HIV has been (f019), since a patient on long-term HIV care is told these counts.
Medication facts: zidovudine and lamivudine continue (three years plus the current regimen); lopinavir–ritonavir was replaced by nevirapine 45 days before presentation.
